extracted.intended_audience: agency staff implementing notice-and-comment procedures; members of the public and regulated parties who submit comments or respond to notices
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for how agencies must give notice, accept, process, retain, and respond to public comments on proposed agency actions, and for how members of the public should submit useful comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing comments in accordance with governing procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary method for participating in notice and comment proceedings is through the filing of comments in accordance with the agency's specified procedures (e.g., "comments in accordance with § 3010.140"). The initiating notice and order will specify the deadline for filing comments and, if provided, reply comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the cited procedural section for format, submission method, and deadlines; check the notice/order for whether reply comments are allowed and for exact deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide notice and 30-day minimum comment period
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies (e.g., Forest Service) shall provide notice to the public of a proposed directive and provide an opportunity to submit comments during a comment period of not less than 30 days, and consider and respond to timely comments received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 30-day minimum comment period is required for proposed directives unless another provision applies; agencies must consider and respond to timely submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of notice may be oral or written; generally written to affected parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice may be oral or written. The Commission will generally provide to manufacturers or private labelers written notice and opportunity to comment on information subject to disclosure under the statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When practicable provide written notice to affected parties; consider oral notice only where appropriate and ensure clear record of what was communicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified comment-period lengths and late comments policy
rubrics_metrics.description: A commenter must file a written comment within the agency's specified calendar days (e.g., 30 calendar days). Agencies may consider late-filed comments if they determine the comment will assist in disposition of the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit within stated period to ensure consideration; agencies have discretion to accept late comments only when they are relevant and helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept electronic (e-mail) and written comments; provide subscription/notice services
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies accept e-mail and written comments on standards and provide opportunities for the public to register for periodic e-mail notices about matters of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the agency's accepted submission channels (email, mail) and consider subscribing to agency notice lists to receive alerts about open comment periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice-and-comment required to the extent practicable; exceptions permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute or regulation requires notice and opportunity to comment 'to the extent practicable' and identifies circumstances when notice and opportunity to comment is not practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should follow notice-and-comment procedures when practicable; document and justify any exceptions where notice is not practicable (e.g., emergencies or confidentiality concerns).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments must follow procedural submission rules for particular proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters may submit comments on applications or proposals in accordance with the procedures set out in the relevant part or chapter (e.g., original and one copy filing requirements with an Applications office).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the specific part/chapter instructions (number of copies, address, forms) and comply exactly to avoid rejection for procedural defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies must receive, consider, and make comments available for inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency practice requires receiving and considering comments, and making comments available for inspection by interested parties upon request; comments must be retained as long as the related action (e.g., restriction) remains in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should maintain public comment files and provide access upon request; public commenters should assume submissions will be publicly available unless exempted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements to publish notice in public venues and on-site postings
rubrics_metrics.description: For certain actions (e.g., airport restrictions) the applicant or agency must publish a notice of the proposed restriction in an areawide publication, post a notice in a prominent location at the facility (e.g., airport), and provide public notice and opportunity for comment as prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use locality-appropriate publications and conspicuous on-site postings to maximize public visibility where regulations require specific publication/posting methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of supporting data and comments related to approved actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must retain all relevant supporting data and all comments relating to an approved restriction for the period specified by the regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain records and comments for the full retention period; ensures transparency and enables future review or FOIA requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice contents in Federal Register notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Register notices of receipt must include notice of the opportunity for public comment and evidence on the request, the date of receipt, and the opportunity for the public to submit comment within the stated timeframe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal Register notices should clearly state procedural elements (what is requested, deadlines, how to submit evidence/comments) so interested parties can meaningfully participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and usefulness of comments: support with documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should be in regard to the information at issue; include documentation where available if the comments are to assist the agency's evaluation. Comments of a general nature (e.g., general suggestions) may be less useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide factual, specific, and documented comments tied to the record to increase the likelihood the agency can use and respond to them; avoid only general or speculative statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of intent to disclose and opportunity for affected party response
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency proposes to disclose information (e.g., under section 6(b) of the CPSA), it must provide notice to the manufacturer or private labeler of the intent to disclose and consider comments submitted under the initial notice before disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affected parties should submit comments under the initial notice to preserve arguments against disclosure; agencies must consider those submissions before final disclosure decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies may shorten notice periods when safety requires
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may provide a lesser period of notice and opportunity to comment where safety requires it (i.e., urgent circumstances justify shortening the usual notice period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must document the safety rationale for shorter periods; commenters should monitor expedited notices and act quickly when shortened periods are announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural handling of replies and recordkeeping in multi-stage processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices and orders initiating proceedings will set deadlines for filing comments and, if provided, reply comments; agencies may require summaries of comments received and may request additional information from applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow deadlines for initial and reply comments, and be prepared to provide summaries or additional requested materials if the rule or application process calls for them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of comments and evidence to interested parties during review processes
rubrics_metrics.description: The public shall have the opportunity to submit comment and evidence on petitions or requests following Federal Register notice, and agencies will make comments available so that interested parties can review submissions relevant to the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interested parties should review the public docket to understand others' positions and evidence; agencies should ensure docket completeness and accessibility.
